Prevention: Prune trees to enhance aeration in fields.
Remove all pruned material from the field and burn it to avoid spread of the pest.
Avoid planting other host plants such as citrus and pineapples near the field
Apply a 15 cm wide band of
Deltamethrin with a brush at the base of the stem (1 foot from the base)
Monitoring: Walk through the field on a weekly basis, Check trees for evidence of pests.
Also check nearby sorrel and pigeon peas as these are known hosts
Institute control measures when scales are first observed on fruits, leaves or trunks.
Direct Control: Spray with agricultural oils once the pest has been seen
Apply agricultural oils at 200 ml per 20 lt of water
Spray with soapy solution (potassium/ insecticidal soaps) (Safer soap)
Add 10-15 tablespoons full of liquid soap in 20 lt bucket of water and spray
Restrictions: Ensure appropriate protection is worn during handling of agrochemical products.
Rotate chemical use to prevent the build-up of resistance to these chemicals
Acetamiprid (Caprid 2.5-5 ml or 1/2-1 tsp per gal. water) which has contact systemic and translaminar activity
Wait for chemical to dry before re-entry.
Pyriproxyfen (Admiral 5-10mls or 1-2 tsp per gal water).
Do not re-enter until chemical has dried.
If swallowed do not induce vomiting give water and call a doctor
Deltamethrin (750 mls in 20 lt of water)
